title: Graphing a Piecewise Linear Sawtooth Function with a Jump
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of the piecewise-defined function g(x) = 1 - x for 0 <= x <= 1, and g(x) = 2 - x for 1 < x <= 2.
finalAnswer: \text{Two parallel segments of slope } -1: \text{ from } (0, 1) \text{ to } (1, 0), \text{ and from } (1, 1) \text{ (open) to } (2, 0)

steps.title: Analyze the First Branch on [0, 1]
steps.explanation: On [0, 1], g(x) = 1 - x is a line segment of slope -1 starting at (0, 1) (closed dot) and ending at (1, 0) (closed dot).
steps.why: Evaluating g(0) = 1 and g(1) = 0 fixes both included endpoints of the first linear piece.

steps.title: Analyze the Second Branch on (1, 2]
steps.explanation: On (1, 2], g(x) = 2 - x is a parallel line segment of slope -1 starting with an open circle at (1, 1) and descending to a closed dot at (2, 0).
steps.why: Because x = 1 is excluded from 1 < x <= 2, the point (1, 2 - 1) = (1, 1) is marked as an open circle.

steps.title: Identify the Jump Discontinuity and Range
steps.explanation: At x = 1, the graph jumps from g(1) = 0 up to the right-hand limit 1, forming two parallel sawtooth segments over [0, 2] with range [0, 1].
steps.why: A piecewise function has a jump discontinuity where the left-hand and right-hand limits at the boundary point are unequal.
